rubric.result: The objective's four promises are all produced by the diff, and the one composition that broke them in attempt 1 is repaired. Shows what the groom will create: the `groomable` branch renders `milestone`, `EpicGroomPanelLabels.planCount(plan.length)` and one `#<order> · <title>` item with its labels. Runs it: `press(EpicGroomClient.groom)`. Shows the issues created with their rung: `groomedIssues` takes `acted.issues` after a press and `read.issues` on a reload, each rendered with `issue.status`. Authorises them: `press(EpicGroomClient.promote)` then the AUTHORISED sentence. Refusals reach the screen untranslated on both channels (`title={read.error}`, `title={refusal.error}`). The repair: the single `asked` state is now two, `acted` and `refusal`, and `press` writes the refusal branch without touching `acted` (`setRefusal(answered)` alone, line 356), so a promotion refused after a successful groom leaves `acted` holding the groomed answer, `groomedIssues` non-null, and line 370's pre-groom branch unreachable because it is guarded by `acted === null`. I traced the compositions the split could have opened and none does: `setActed` is always paired with `setRefusal(null)` (lines 353-354), so a refusal banner cannot survive a later successful press — groom refused then groom pressed again successfully clears it, promotion refused then promotion pressed again successfully clears it and lands on the `authorised` branch, which renders no banner at all; `read` is frozen at a resting kind while any of this happens (`RESTING_KINDS` in `useEpicGroom.ts` returns without rescheduling), so nothing rewrites it underneath; and `acted` cannot be set without a key, since `press` returns early on `gateKey === null`.

The `**TDD:**` line names `it('shows what the groom will create before anything is created')` and fixes the assertion: with `EpicGroomMother.groomable()`, the milestone, the count and every planned issue's order, title and labels on screen, and no request posted. The test in the diff asserts exactly that over exactly that input — `findByText(EpicGroomMother.MILESTONE)`, `getByText('2 issues')` (the mother's plan holds two), `'#1 · The intermediate gate retires'` and `'#2 · The session channel'` with `GATE_ISSUE.labels.join(', ')` and `CHANNEL_ISSUE.labels.join(', ')`, and `expect(reading).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)`, the single GET, which is what pins 'no request has been posted'. Its declared boundary pair `it('pressing the groom sends the key and then shows the issues it created')` is present and asserts the literal POST `('/epic-groom', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'x-gate-key': EpicGroomMother.KEY } })` followed by the created issues. Unchanged from attempt 1 and still the assertion the plan wrote.

The single `Contract (…EpicGroomPanel.tsx)` block declares ten constants; all ten are in the diff with the same names and byte-identical values (lines 294-303), and every one has a use: GROOM/GROOMING and PROMOTE/PROMOTING as each button's in-flight pair, WILL_CREATE and CREATED over the two lists, AUTHORISED in the authorised branch, ONLY_FROM_THE_PAGE as the no-key notice, UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE as the `backend-unreachable` banner, HEADING on every `Panel`. No `Current state`, `Call site` or `Final text` block accompanies this task. The shapes the panel consumes still match the committed contract on the other side: `EpicGroomOutcome` / `EpicGroomAskOutcome` in `EpicGroom.types.ts` (the new `EpicGroomActed` and `EpicGroomAskRefusal` aliases are `Extract`/`Exclude` over that same union, so they cannot drift from it), and `EpicGroomClient.groom/promote(key: string)` matches the `press` parameter type.

Rows the diff bears on, all implemented with the value the row states. D-6: the gate is two buttons the program answers for, no conversational path. D-22: both presses go through `press`, which refuses with no key and sends `x-gate-key`, and a refusal is displayed rather than routed around — the repair strengthens this row rather than touching it, since a refused gate now leaves the true state on screen instead of an inviting pre-groom button. D-7: exactly two buttons exist, groom and promotion; nothing writes to a pull request and there is no merge button. D-23: `awaiting-publication` is in `NOTHING_TO_SHOW_KINDS` and renders `null`, leaving gate 1's panel to say the groom waits for the merge. D-21: the panel renders only its own `Panel` or `null` and touches no other region of the page. D-13: every branch derives from the `GET /epic-groom` read or from the press's own answer; nothing is persisted. No row is reopened.

Exemplars: the panel still follows `SpecFreezePanel.tsx` — the same `useRef` + `useState` press guard, `Panel heading=`, `Banner type="error" role="alert" title={…}` with the detail untranslated, `Button` with `disabled` and an in-flight label — and the CSS follows `SpecFreezePanel.css` (BEM under `epic-groom-panel__`, `margin: 0`, `var(--foreground-secondary)`, flex column lists with `list-style: none`); every class the CSS declares is used by the TSX, and only the `system-ui/{banner,button,panel}` mirrors are consumed, with no raw `<button>`/`<h2>` and no edit under `system-ui/theme/`. Where the diff now departs from the exemplar it departs towards the rule: `SpecFreezePanel` keeps one `asked` state, this panel keeps `acted` and `refusal` apart, which is what makes a refusal stop erasing a result. `frontend/README.md`'s yardstick holds by reading (names in English, zero prose, no `export default`, no `../` import, Spanish confined to the label constants, which `style.md` exempts as product copy). `conventions/style.md`: the previous low is repaired in the idiom that was named for it — the three label formatters now hang off `EpicGroomPanelLabels` (lines 320-324) and are reached as `EpicGroomPanelLabels.planCount/planItem/issueItem`, the same object-namespace form `EpicGroomClient` uses next door in `client.ts` and `EpicGroomMother` uses in `__scenarios__`, so the file now reads like its siblings; no finding is repeated here. `conventions/architecture.md`, `domain.md`, `boundaries.md`: the panel is the outermost edge of the front end, reaches the backend only through the already-built `EpicGroomClient`, forms no second opinion about what arrived and crosses no layer the wrong way. `conventions/decisions.md`: `NOTHING_TO_SHOW_KINDS` and `useEpicGroom`'s `RESTING_KINDS` still answer two different questions (what this panel renders vs. when the hook stops polling), so idiom, not one decision written twice. `conventions/simplicity.md`: every branch answers a state the brief names; the trailing `return null` (line 445) is unreachable today and is the return the language requires. `conventions/defects.md`, rule by rule — (1) closed vocabulary: no loose-string classification is introduced; the dispatch is over the closed unions `EpicGroomOutcome['kind']` and `EpicGroomAskOutcome['kind']`, and the new `Extract`/`Exclude` aliases tighten it, since `askBanner` can no longer be reached by an `acted` value at all; the chain still ends in `null` rather than a `never` check, so a member added later would fall through silently — recorded, as in attempt 1, not a finding, because it is the exemplar's own form and no member falls through today; (2) raw map as the return value of logic: no subject, the panel returns JSX and passes typed value objects; (3) two fields that have to agree: `isPressing`/`isPressingRef` are written and cleared together inside `press` and exist because React state is asynchronous, the exemplar's double-press guard; `acted` and `refusal` are not a pair that must agree — they are two independent facts (the last result, the last refusal) and every combination of them is meaningful, which is precisely the defect the split removed; no sentinel stands for an absence, an absent key is `null` in the type and an absent press is `null`; (4) an error named for where it happens: no subject, this diff declares no error type. No document of either yardstick prescribes a delivery shape for a new frontend panel, and the file is wired into the page by task 13, so nothing is left on an old path.

Does not apply: this item's subject is a pre-existing test that ended up asserting less, and the diff has none. The four frontend files are `new file mode 100644` with no `-` line at all. The only `-` line in the whole package is in the plan markdown — `there is nothing to show while gate 1 has not been pressed`. reflowed to end in a comma so an eighth name could follow it — which touches no assertion, case or test, and is judged under `alcance` as an amendment.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code. `EpicGroomPanel.tsx` is the only production file (with its CSS and its barrel); the tests double nothing of the app — they stub `fetch`, the real external boundary, with bodies from `__scenarios__/EpicGroomMother.ts`, and everything between that boundary and the screen is real: the real `EpicGroomClient` parses the body, the real `useEpicGroom` polls and rests, the real component renders. The repair in particular lives in production: the new test's assertions depend on `acted` surviving the refusal in `EpicGroomPanel.tsx`, not on anything the test set up — the mother is unchanged and the third stubbed response is the same `notFromThePage()` the older refusal test already used. Assertions are on rendered DOM text and on the literal request sent at the boundary; reverting the component takes all eight tests red.

The four frontend paths are exactly the four `**Files:**` declares, all `(create)` and all new, and inside them every line traces to a sentence of the task: the `null` rungs, the three rendering branches, the disabled rule and the ONLY_FROM_THE_PAGE notice, both banners, the BEM CSS, the barrel. Nothing named in `### Out of scope` is touched, and the wiring into `Home` is correctly absent (task 13 owns it). The fifth path is an amendment to the plan, and I read the hunk line by line: it adds one name to this task's `**Tests:**` list, `a promotion refused after a successful groom keeps the groomed issues on screen`, and changes nothing else — not `**Files:**`, not `**TDD:**`, not `**Verification:**`, not any other task. It is justified and it is the honest direction: the test exists because the ordered repair required it, and `plan-tasks.js` reads test names out of `**Tests:**`, so declaring it makes the control require the test rather than disarm anything.

Eight new tests, all in `EpicGroomPanel.test.tsx`; the eighth is the repair's. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no randomness, no sleep, no real network — `fetch` is stubbed per test with `mockResolvedValueOnce` chains and every wait goes through `findBy*`/`waitFor`, never a timeout; the hook's 10 s timer is only reached in the `draft` case and is cleared by the effect's teardown on unmount. Isolated: each test stubs its own `fetch` with fresh `Response` instances, `afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllGlobals())` undoes it, RTL's automatic cleanup unmounts between tests, and nothing depends on file order. Verifies real behaviour: the assertions are on what the component renders and on the literal request the real client sent. I checked specifically that the new test can fail for the reason its name gives: with the split reverted to a single `asked` state, the refusal would overwrite the groom's result, `acted` would be null, line 370's `groomable` branch would match, and all four of its assertions fall — `#348 · …` and `#349 · …` absent, the promotion button absent, and the groom button back on screen, which is exactly what `expect(screen.queryByRole('button', GROOM_BUTTON)).not.toBeInTheDocument()` pins. The two intermediate awaits (`findByRole` for each button) also make it fail rather than hang if the sequence breaks earlier. I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` and its `testing-anti-patterns.md` reference for the finer half: none of its anti-patterns is present — no assertion on a `*-mock` element, no test-only path in production, mock setup shorter than the test body, and the mother's bodies mirror the wire shape the backend routes send. Its 'One thing. "and" in name? Split it.' would bite several names including the new one, but those names were written verbatim by the plan (`**TDD:**` and `**Tests:**`, the eighth added by the amendment to match the ordered repair), so the implementer could not have written anything else: a clash between a control of the plan and the yardstick, declared here and left out of the findings.
